title: Three components, three normalizations: the front end decides authentication on a path the back end never opens
index_line: T-0045 · AUTH_DECISION · nginx sets an auth header for a path, Apache re-normalizes to a different file · any-proxy-chain · corroborated
invariant_violated: A request is assumed to be one object that each layer agrees on. It is not: the front-end proxy normalizes the path to choose an access rule, and the back-end server normalizes the same bytes again to choose a file. Where the two normalizations differ, the rule is applied to one path and the script that runs is another.

mechanism.does: the attacker requests a path built so that two normalizers disagree — encoded octets, duplicate slashes, dot segments, case
the front-end proxy normalizes the path, matches it against its location rules, and concludes this request needs no authentication
the proxy records that conclusion as a header for the backend and forwards the *original* path
the backend re-normalizes the same bytes to a different file and resolves it to a PHP script that expects to be protected
the backend honours the proxy's header rather than re-deriving the decision, so the script executes for an unauthenticated caller
the script performs an authenticated action on the attacker's behalf

source.http.request.value: the request path — the payload is a normalization difference, not a traversal the backend would accept on its own

proxy.desync.value: the front-end/back-end disagreement — here about *which file* the path names, rather than where the request ends

encoding.path.value: `//`, `/.`, `%2e`, `/./`, case, and trailing-dot forms; the working value is whatever the two normalizers split on

guard.none.value: the authorization decision is transported as a header produced upstream and consumed downstream, with no re-derivation

preconditions.expr: the management interface is served through two normalizing layers (a reverse proxy in front of an application server)
the upstream's decision travels to the backend as a header rather than being re-evaluated
the backend resolves a PHP script for a path the front end classified as unauthenticated

check.spec: compare the file each layer resolves for a set of mutation payloads; a mismatch is the bug

success: an unauthenticated request returns a script's output rather than a login page
the same path fails when the proxy's location rule is tightened — the differential proves the rule is what was bypassed
requests that differ only in normalization reach different handlers with the same authorization verdict
failure_like: the backend re-derives authorization from its own view of the path
the proxy rejects or canonicalises the mutation before the backend sees it
false_positive: a login page returned with status 200 — read the body, not the code
an unauthenticated endpoint that is *meant* to be public (the static assets, the login handler itself)

hazards: the audit unit is (path mutations) × (layers) — build a matrix and compare which file each layer resolves; that is a 20-minute test with curl
this class is invisible to source review because no single component is wrong: each normalizes consistently with itself
the fix is a re-derivation at the backend, not a better regex in the proxy
CWE-288 'alternate path or channel' is the right label and the right search: look for any endpoint reachable by a second route
non_transfers: single-layer servers that resolve and authorize in one step
chains whose backend re-checks authorization from its own resolution

evidence.target: PAN-OS management web interface, nginx + Apache + PHP (CVE-2025-0108)
